Senses.Explanation: The parent image names verbal entanglement in Chan records, but this exact compound is very thin and occurs only in late framing prose. Gao Shitai's prefatory verse praises the record owner for effacing forms and cutting vine-tangle; a preface says that Linji's staff and shout cut all vine-tangle; a biographical preface pairs cutting vine-tangle with destroying thorn thickets. The Zen deviation comes from the established Chan use of creepers for entangling words, here made the object of cutting. Unlike more common longer forms that add an explicit verb of severing, the exact phrase is not attested in this concordance as a live-exchange command, so this entry does not present it as one.
